# paceifier

> Paced versions of the standard collection methods for Node.js, Deno and Bun. A long synchronous loop runs in slices of about 1 ms, and the event loop gets a turn between slices, so I/O, timers and other requests keep running while the job works. Zero dependencies, CommonJS and ESM, TypeScript types included.

Use it when a server runs a long CPU-bound loop over many items (CSV or XML rows, database records, entries of a large Map) and other requests must not wait for it. Don't use it for short jobs, for one call that can't be split (a single JSON.parse of a huge string), or for work that should finish as fast as possible on another core (use worker_threads).

Install with `npm install paceifier`. Every method takes any iterable and a synchronous `fn(item, index)`, and returns a promise.

```js
const { mapPaced, forEachPaced, pace } = require('paceifier'); // or import { … } from 'paceifier'

const lines = await mapPaced(rows, (row, index) => format(row));
await forEachPaced(map.values(), entry => work(entry));

// Low-level: pace() returns undefined while the slice has time left,
// or a promise to await. Await it directly.
for (const item of items) {
	const pause = pace();
	if (pause) await pause;
	work(item);
}
```

Methods: forEachPaced, mapPaced, filterPaced, flatMapPaced, reducePaced, findPaced, findIndexPaced, somePaced, everyPaced. They behave like the Array methods of the same name without the suffix. `require('paceifier/register')` adds them to Array.prototype and Iterator.prototype as non-enumerable methods, for example `await rows.mapPaced(format)`.

Cost is about 75 ns per item plus a few microseconds per pause. With items of a few microseconds or more, a job is 2 to 5% slower than a blocking loop, and the event loop never waits much longer than 1 ms. Supported runtimes are Node.js 22+, Deno 2.9+ and Bun 1.2+.
